pathway.title: Post Holdings, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The business is large and spread widely enough to give reasonable cash-flow visibility, but reported growth overstates underlying demand. Net sales were USD 8,412.5 million over the last twelve months across four segments, and no customer exceeds 17.4% of sales, yet pet food supplied USD 890.6 million, or 76.3%, of the USD 1,167.1 million rise in sales between fiscal 2023 and fiscal 2025, and in nine months to June 2026 Post Consumer Brands sales fell 8.6% without 8th Avenue while pet food sales fell 15.0%. Creditors are relying on acquired earnings that are already shrinking organically. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_post-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 157; 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 33; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C21; calculation C22; calculation C23

Pricing power is limited and buyers hold most of the leverage. The largest customers are 29.9% of Post Consumer Brands, 33.0% of Weetabix, 42.0% of Foodservice and 34.9% of Refrigerated Retail, management expects the ready-to-eat cereal category to stay weak, and pet food prices fell on mix and promotion. Eggs are the exception only because avian influenza outbreaks lifted prices: that pricing raised Foodservice profit by USD 91.6 million, or 29.7%, in fiscal 2025 and is now lapping, so third-quarter Foodservice sales fell 6.5% and its profit fell 18.6%. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_post-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 76, 155; 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 26, 33–34; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ex99-1q32026er.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C24; calculation C25

Margins have held at group level, but the mix beneath them is moving and the main cost pressures are external. Reported EBITDA margin was 16.0% in fiscal 2024, 16.3% in fiscal 2025 and 16.4% over the last twelve months, helped in the nine months to June 2026 by USD 198.0 million of lower raw material costs in Foodservice, mainly eggs. Tariffs and the conflict in Iran have raised input, energy and freight costs, and management plans USD 80 million to USD 90 million of cage-free and precooked egg expansion, so margins depend on items management does not control. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_post-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 29, 34; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ex99-1q32026er.htm.jsonl, page 7; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C15

Cash conversion is moderate and flattered in the latest period because capital spending fell. Free cash flow was USD 553.1 million over the last twelve months, 40.0% of reported EBITDA against 36.7% in fiscal 2025, after USD 439.5 million of capital expenditure and USD 370.1 million of cash interest in fiscal 2025. Nine-month free cash flow rose to USD 401.5 million from USD 336.5 million because additions to property fell, not because operating cash flow rose, and the split of capital spending between maintenance and growth is not stated. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_post-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 96, 128; 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C14

Leverage is high and barely falling, and cover is thinner than the issuer's own ratios suggest. Net debt of USD 7,367.0 million at June 30, 2026 is 5.33x reported EBITDA, or USD 7,406.3 million and 5.36x pro forma for USD 39.3 million of repurchases between July 1 and August 5, 2026, against 5.45x at September 30, 2025. The issuer reports 4.6x net leverage and 3.8x interest cover on credit-agreement Adjusted EBITDA, but add-backs are 16.84% of reported EBITDA, reported EBITDA covered interest expense 3.30x over the last twelve months, and principal debt rose USD 223.8 million in nine months. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 17; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ex99-1q32026er.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 22; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C9; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C11

Liquidity and the near maturity profile are the main supports, and the longer wall is the refinancing risk. Cash and undrawn revolver capacity were USD 1,242.4 million at June 30, 2026 before the later repurchases, 2.16x the USD 576.3 million falling due in fiscal 2027, of which USD 575.0 million is convertible notes due in August 2027 with a conversion price about 19.5% above the average price Post paid for shares after the quarter end. USD 4,566.0 million, or 59.5% of principal, falls due in fiscal 2030 to fiscal 2033, and refinancing the two lowest-coupon issues at the 6.50% coupon of the December 2025 notes would add about USD 45.6 million of interest a year. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18, 20–21; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ex99-1q32026er.htm.jsonl, page 6; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C18; calculation C19; calculation C20

Financial policy is the weakest dimension. Cash repurchases ran at 2.28x free cash flow in nine months to June 2026 and 1.45x in fiscal 2025, the board has approved four authorizations since August 2025, no leverage target is stated, and no sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed to support or constrain the issuer. Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk as Medium, and the one financial covenant tests secured net leverage only when revolver usage passes 30% of commitments, so it is untested at current usage. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 23; 10-K_2025-09-30_post-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 96; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C14; calculation C32

The realistic downside is leverage drifting up on lower egg earnings, not a liquidity event. If Foodservice earnings fell back to the USD 500 million run rate management describes and about USD 20 million of divested earnings left, Adjusted EBITDA would settle near management's comparable fiscal 2027 base of about USD 1.48 billion, USD 135.9 million or 8.4% below the last twelve months. With pro forma net debt of USD 7,406.3 million unchanged, reported-basis net leverage would rise from 5.36x to 5.94x, and free cash flow would fall to about USD 417.2 million, so using the USD 490.7 million of authorization left would exceed it by USD 73.5 million. Liquidity still covers the 2027 convertible notes, and management can stop repurchases, trim capital spending toward the USD 370 million to USD 390 million guided for fiscal 2026, or sell facilities, so distress is not the expected outcome. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ex99-1q32026er.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 21; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C29; calculation C30; calculation C31; calculation C17; calculation C4

Over 12 months to 24 months the outlook is flat earnings, with the convertible notes due in August 2027 the one dated test. Management narrowed fiscal 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to USD 1,560 million to USD 1,570 million, which implies a fourth quarter of USD 369.5 million to USD 379.5 million against USD 425.4 million a year earlier, and describes fiscal 2027 as generally flat on a comparable base. Tailwinds are lower egg costs, Weetabix margin gains and lower capital spending; headwinds are pet food distribution losses, a weak cereal category, higher coupons on refinanced debt and the refinancing wall in fiscal 2030 to fiscal 2033. Over 3 years to 5 years the open questions are whether cereal and pet food volumes stabilise and whether that wall is refinanced at coupons above those it replaces. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ex99-1q32026er.htm.jsonl, pages 4–7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 34; calculation C28; calculation C29; calculation C18; calculation C19

cells.text: Calculated: cash plus the revolver's available capacity

runs.text: Liquidity covers the nearest maturity twice over. Cash and undrawn revolver capacity of USD 1,242.4 million compare with USD 576.3 million due in fiscal 2027, so a cash-settled convertible does not depend on market access and no refinancing is forced in the next twelve months. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 21; calculation C17

Scale and customer spread cushion a single shock. Net sales of USD 8,412.5 million come from four segments and the largest customer is 17.4% of sales, so the loss of one account or one product line is partly absorbed by the others. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_post-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C1

Cash generation is steady. Free cash flow of USD 553.1 million, 40.0% of reported EBITDA, covers interest and capital spending with a surplus that would repay debt if repurchases stopped. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C12; calculation C13

Shareholder returns outrun cash generation. Cash repurchases were 2.28x free cash flow in nine months while principal debt rose USD 223.8 million, so each further quarter at that pace adds to net debt and delays deleveraging. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 17; calculation C14; calculation C11

Leverage is high and the fall from 5.45x to 5.33x is small. Net debt of USD 7,367.0 million, USD 7,406.3 million pro forma, leaves little room for an earnings decline: a fall of USD 135.9 million in EBITDA would lift reported-basis net leverage to 5.94x. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C4; calculation C29; calculation C30

Organic sales are shrinking in the largest segment. Post Consumer Brands sales fell 8.6% in nine months without 8th Avenue and pet food sales fell 15.0%, so acquired earnings erode and revenue visibility is lower than the headline suggests. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 33; calculation C22; calculation C23

Earnings lean on an egg price cycle. Foodservice produced 38.5% of nine-month segment profit and management puts about USD 60 million of its fiscal 2026 earnings above a USD 500 million run rate, so a reversal lowers EBITDA without any change in debt. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 26; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ex99-1q32026er.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C26; calculation C29

Refinancing will cost more. The 2030 and 2031 senior notes carry lower coupons than the 6.50% paid in December 2025, and refinancing them at that coupon would add about USD 45.6 million of interest a year against interest that already takes 30.3% of reported EBITDA. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 19; calculation C19; calculation C10

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Post reshaped its portfolio in both directions over the last two years. It bought the pet food business of J. M. Smucker in April 2023 for USD 1,207.5 million, partly paid in newly issued Post shares valued at USD 492.3 million, bought Perfection Pet Foods for USD 235.0 million in December 2023, and in fiscal 2025 bought Potato Products of Idaho for USD 120.0 million and the rest of 8th Avenue for USD 798.8 million, which included retiring its debt and was funded with cash and revolver borrowings. It then sold 8th Avenue's pasta business on December 1, 2025 for a preliminary USD 375.0 million, receiving USD 378.5 million at closing while the buyer took on USD 78.2 million of leaseback liabilities, and sold Crystal Farms on May 1, 2026 for a preliminary USD 50.0 million, receiving USD 45.7 million at closing. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_post-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 117–119; 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 12; calculation C17; calculation C16

Three note issues since October 2024 pushed maturities out and raised either coupons or principal. On October 9, 2024 Post issued USD 600.0 million of senior notes due 2034 at par and used part of the proceeds to redeem its notes due 2028. On December 15, 2025 it issued USD 1,300.0 million of 6.50% notes due 2036 at par and redeemed all USD 1,235.0 million of its 5.50% notes due 2029 for a premium of USD 22.6 million, a coupon 1.00 percentage points higher. On March 13, 2026 it issued a further USD 600.0 million of the 2034 notes at 100.75% of par and used the proceeds to repay the revolver. The notes are guaranteed by the domestic subsidiaries other than immaterial, excluded and unrestricted ones. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_post-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 79, 136; 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20, 22; calculation C19

Two events after the quarter end are kept outside the period figures. Post repurchased shares for USD 39.3 million between July 1 and August 5, 2026, leaving USD 490.7 million of authorization, and it expects to sell its Cobourg and Ashton-under-Lyne facilities in the second half of calendar 2026, with no proceeds stated. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ex99-1q32026er.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: This answer covers the financial foundation of Post Holdings, Inc. as of 2026-11-05. The pathway is the credit snapshot. The scope is the issuer's statements, debt, leverage, coverage and liquidity from the supplied filings and releases through the quarter ended June 30, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Post's gross leverage is 5.52x reported EBITDA, little changed in nine months, because USD 916.1 million of repurchases absorbed free cash flow and divestiture proceeds; creditors rely on cash generation and revolver access, not debt reduction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; calculation C47; calculation C35; calculation C98

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cost is the pressure point: interest expense, net rose to USD 419.1 million over the last twelve months from USD 361.4 million in fiscal 2025, and reported EBITDA covered fiscal 2025 cash interest 3.59x. Liquidity is adequate at USD 1,242.4 million of cash and undrawn revolver, with the next debt maturity, USD 576.3 million, in fiscal 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_post-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; calculation C68; calculation C52; calculation C72; calculation C54

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Gross debt at carrying value rose to USD 7,632.6 million at June 30, 2026 from USD 7,422.9 million at September 30, 2025, while last-twelve-months reported EBITDA rose to USD 1,383.0 million from USD 1,330.1 million. Gross leverage therefore eased from 5.58x to 5.52x and net leverage from 5.45x to 5.33x. The larger step was in fiscal 2025, when net leverage rose from 4.76x to 5.45x as USD 920.3 million of acquisitions and USD 709.0 million of repurchases were paid from cash and borrowings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_post-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 94–96; 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C47; calculation C35; calculation C48; calculation C36; calculation C34; calculation C76

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fiscal 2026 refinancings raised principal debt rather than holding it flat. USD 1,300.0 million of 6.50% notes due 2036 and USD 600.0 million of additional senior notes due 2034 repaid USD 1,235.0 million of 5.50% notes due 2029 and the revolver, which lengthened the profile at higher coupons, but principal still rose by USD 223.8 million to USD 7,676.0 million, and net debt rose USD 120.8 million over nine months despite USD 424.2 million of disposal proceeds.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 17–22; calculation C77; calculation C75

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Coverage is thinner than leverage suggests. Reported EBITDA covered cash interest 3.59x in fiscal 2025 against 3.94x in fiscal 2024, and interest expense, net is up USD 57.7 million over the last twelve months on higher average debt, a higher average rate and lower interest income, so cover on that basis eased from 3.68x to 3.30x. Cash interest paid is not printed for any fiscal 2026 period, so interim cash cover is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_post-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 94, 128; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ex99-1q32026er.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C52; calculation C51; calculation C78; calculation C79; calculation C80

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow improved because capital expenditure fell, not because operations improved. Over nine months operating cash flow was USD 691.3 million against USD 697.0 million, additions to property were USD 289.8 million against USD 360.5 million, and free cash flow was USD 401.5 million against USD 336.5 million. Cash paid for repurchases of USD 916.1 million was more than twice that free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; calculation C84; calculation C83; calculation C98

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is the offset. Cash of USD 265.6 million plus USD 976.8 million of available revolver capacity gives USD 1,242.4 million, against USD 714.4 million at September 30, 2025, because the March 2026 notes repaid the revolver. No debt falls due before fiscal 2027, when USD 576.3 million matures, led by USD 575.0 million of convertible notes due in August 2027; the revolver matures in 2029. The one financial covenant tests secured net leverage and applies only when revolver usage passes 30% of commitments, so it is untested at current usage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 17–23; calculation C72; calculation C73; calculation C54

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: These ratios are not the issuer's own. The issuer reports net leverage of 4.6x on principal debt of USD 7,676.0 million less cash, over Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,597.3 million after credit-agreement adjustments of USD 18.6 million. Issuer add-backs are 16.84% of reported EBITDA, which is why adjusted leverage of 4.56x net and reported leverage of 5.33x net differ so widely. The secured net leverage ratio the covenant tests is not reported, so covenant headroom is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ex99-1q32026er.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22; 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation C50; calculation C48; calculation C89; calculation C90; calculation C91

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Obligations outside the debt figure are mostly commitments, not borrowings. At September 30, 2025, operating lease liabilities of USD 277.9 million would add 0.21x to gross leverage if counted as debt, signed leases not yet started carry USD 138.3 million of future payments, and minimum purchase commitments are USD 7,382.7 million, mainly egg contracts and open purchase orders. The balance sheet carries pension assets of USD 151.6 million and pension and retiree benefit obligations of USD 57.3 million, lease guarantees on the former Bob Evans restaurants carry USD 13.5 million of annual rent, and litigation is not expected to be material. None of these is in Total Debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Subsequent events are kept out of the period figures. Repurchases of USD 39.3 million after June 30, 2026 lift pro forma net leverage to 5.36x, and two facility sales expected in the second half of calendar 2026 are not reflected because no proceeds are stated. Several events carry more than one figure, and the definition register sets each out with its role: the 8th Avenue acquisition, the pasta sale and the Crystal Farms sale. No supplier finance, factoring or deferred-revenue float appears in the statements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ex99-1q32026er.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 9–12; calculation C57; calculation C58

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against a cautious view is liquidity and a clear runway: USD 1,242.4 million of cash and undrawn revolver, no revolver drawings, and no maturity before fiscal 2027. It would win if the next two quarters show repurchases curtailed and free cash flow, USD 553.1 million over the last twelve months, applied to debt, so that net debt fell below USD 7,246.2 million. The view would turn more negative if fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA lands in the USD 369.5 million to USD 379.5 million range the fiscal 2026 outlook implies, against USD 425.4 million a year earlier, because last-twelve-months EBITDA and cover would then fall without any reduction in debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ex99-1q32026er.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; calculation C72; calculation C71; calculation C87; calculation C88

fields.value: The latest balance sheet is dated June 30, 2026 and nothing later is supplied, so every position and ratio describes that date, and the fiscal 2026 year-end is not covered.

fields.value: Reported EBITDA is calculated from net earnings, interest, tax and depreciation and amortization because the issuer prints no unadjusted EBITDA; the issuer's Adjusted EBITDA appears only in the earnings releases, from fiscal 2025 onward.

fields.value: - The latest balance sheet is dated June 30, 2026 and no document after August 6, 2026 is supplied, so net debt, leverage and liquidity describe that date and nothing covers the fiscal year ended September 30, 2026; severity High; the fiscal 2026 annual report or fourth-quarter release would close it.

fields.value: - Cash interest paid is printed for fiscal years only, so cover on cash interest is not established for any interim date; severity Medium; supplemental cash flow data for the interim periods would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The secured net leverage ratio that the covenant tests is not printed, so covenant headroom is not calculable and the issuer's net leverage of 4.6x cannot be compared with the 4.25x test; severity Medium; the credit agreement definitions or a compliance calculation would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Adjusted EBITDA is printed only in the earnings releases and only from fiscal 2025, so adjusted leverage and cover for fiscal 2024 and earlier are not calculable; severity Medium; earlier release reconciliations would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No year-by-year maturity table is printed for June 30, 2026, and the only table, dated September 30, 2025, is superseded by the December 2025 redemption and the new notes; the ladder is built from instrument maturity dates and places the leaseback financial liabilities at the end of their term; severity Medium; a current maturity schedule would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The ranking of the leaseback financial liabilities and the municipal bond is not stated, so both are left out of the debt stack, and equal rank of the revolver and the senior secured notes rests only on the title of a pari passu intercreditor agreement listed in the exhibit index and not supplied; severity Medium; the intercreditor and collateral agreements would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Instrument carrying values are not disclosed at June 30, 2026, although the annual report prints the convertible notes at earlier year-ends; the instrument register carries principal and one financing cost adjustment that reconciles to Total Debt; severity Low; no action is needed beyond the existing debt note.

fields.value: - Lines printed as a dash are carried as not supplied rather than zero, and lines printed in some filings but not others, such as impairment of goodwill, premium from issuance of debt and proceeds from sale of business, are carried as not supplied for the filings that omit them; severity Low; no action is needed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Balance sheets at December 31, 2024, March 31, 2025 and June 30, 2025 are not printed, so leverage at those dates is not calculable; severity Low; the earlier quarterly reports would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Capital expenditure is not split into maintenance and growth, so additions to property are used as total capital expenditure; severity Low; no action is needed beyond the existing note.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The earlier Source readiness work lists only a guarantee and collateral agreement under intercreditor documents; the exhibit index also lists a pari passu intercreditor agreement, which is likewise not supplied, and this answer uses that listing; severity Low; the agreement would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leases, purchase commitments, pensions and guarantees are printed only in the annual report, at September 30, 2025, and are not updated in the quarterly reports; severity Low; the fiscal 2026 annual report would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proceeds of the two facility sales expected in the second half of calendar 2026 are not stated, so the pro forma table makes no adjustment for them; severity Low; filings dated after August 6, 2026 would close it.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: This answer covers the business, ownership, transactions and governance of Post Holdings, Inc. (issuer id post) as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. It draws on the seven supplied filings and releases, the latest dated 2026-08-06, and on the Source readiness work. No sponsor, rating or market data is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Post Holdings is a publicly owned food group with no disclosed controlling holder, so creditors rely on board discipline over buybacks and acquisitions, and repurchases of USD 916.1 million in nine months to June 2026 ran at 2.28x free cash flow of USD 401.5 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-09-30_post-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 161; calculation C9; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The operating base is spread over four segments and no customer exceeds 17.4% of sales, but nine-month pet food sales fell 15.0% and management treats about USD 60 million of Foodservice earnings as above a normal run rate. Sponsor and governance risk is Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_post-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 33; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ex99-1q32026er.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No controlling shareholder or sponsor is disclosed, which removes both a source of equity support and a source of extraction, and leaves the board and the debt covenants as the only limits on shareholder returns. The share count fell 15.7% between November 2025 and August 2026. Two board appointments were announced in February 2026, taking the board to nine, one of them the former Chief Operating Officer, and the chief executive became chairman in December 2025. Beneficial ownership, board independence and pay sit in the proxy statement, which is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_post-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 20, 161; 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-02-03_ex99-1q12026er.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns have outgrown the cash the business generates, and this is the main creditor-relevant behaviour. Cash paid for repurchases was 0.87x free cash flow in fiscal 2023, 0.60x in fiscal 2024, 1.45x in fiscal 2025 and 2.28x in the nine months to June 2026, a period in which principal debt rose USD 223.8 million and book equity fell USD 674.6 million, or 17.9%. The board approved four repurchase authorizations between August 2025 and May 2026, and the two most recent replaced programmes that still had USD 122.1 million and USD 236.6 million unused. The documents do not say how the repurchases were funded.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_post-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 70, 96; 10-Q_2025-12-31_post-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 4, 17, 48; EX-99.1_2026-02-03_ex99-1q12026er.htm.jsonl, page 6; EX-99.1_2026-05-05_ex99-1q22026er.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C13; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Portfolio changes are large against the earnings base and make reported history hard to compare. Post bought the rest of 8th Avenue for USD 798.8 million in July 2025, sold its pasta business five months later for a preliminary USD 375.0 million, and sold Crystal Farms in May 2026 for a preliminary USD 50.0 million after a USD 43.3 million loss on the held-for-sale value. Disposal proceeds of USD 424.2 million in nine months compare with USD 920.3 million spent on acquisitions in fiscal 2025, and goodwill and intangibles are 59.3% of total assets, so the carrying value of the balance sheet rests heavily on past acquisitions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_post-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 96, 117–118; 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 4, 10, 12; calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C18; calculation C28

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings are steady in total but lean on one segment and one price cycle. Foodservice produced 38.5% of nine-month segment profit, up USD 56.6 million on USD 198.0 million of lower raw material costs, mainly eggs, and management says about USD 60 million of its fiscal 2026 earnings sits above a normal run rate of USD 500 million, with preliminary fiscal 2027 Adjusted EBITDA generally flat at about USD 1.48 billion on a comparable basis. Post Consumer Brands grew 9.0% only because 8th Avenue added USD 504.0 million; without it, segment net sales fell 8.6%, with pet food down 15.0%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 26, 33–34; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ex99-1q32026er.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 7; calculation C6; calculation C8; calculation C24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer and category concentration is moderate for the group and high inside each segment. Walmart is 17.4% of net sales and no other customer exceeds 10%, but the largest customers are 29.9% of Post Consumer Brands, 33.0% of Weetabix, 42.0% of Foodservice and 34.9% of Refrigerated Retail, and cereal, eggs and pet food together were 81.3% of fiscal 2025 net sales. Management describes the ready-to-eat cereal category as weak and expects that to continue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure is good enough for monitoring but leaves the legal limits on creditor protection untested. The auditor's opinions on the statements and on internal controls were unqualified, results are released with each filing and non-GAAP measures are reconciled. Against that, 8th Avenue was left out of the controls assessment, the audit matter on Weetabix goodwill records fair value only 8.7% above carrying value, and the indentures and credit agreement that set the limits on distributions are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Related-party dealings are small. BellRing, which shares officers and directors with Post, bought USD 57.5 million of protein shakes in fiscal 2025, purchases from the former affiliate 8th Avenue ended when it was acquired, and no sponsor, monitoring or advisory fee is disclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against caution is that the board's choices have so far kept the balance sheet orderly: no dividend is paid, no sponsor fee is disclosed, the 2028 and 2029 maturities were refinanced early in October 2024 and December 2025, and repurchases are discretionary and can stop. Risk would move to Low if repurchases fell to the level of free cash flow, USD 401.5 million over nine months, and principal debt began to fall, or if the proxy statement showed an independent board and a stated leverage target. It would move to High if the board again outspent free cash flow in the fourth quarter while USD 575.0 million of convertible notes fall due in August 2027, or if egg earnings fell back to the USD 500 million run rate before replacement earnings arrived.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - 8th Avenue's profit is not reported separately after the acquisition, only its net sales of USD 504.0 million over nine months, so the return on the USD 798.8 million price cannot be assessed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Post reshaped its portfolio in both directions over the last two years. It bought the pet food business of J. M. Smucker in April 2023 for USD 1,207.5 million, partly paid in newly issued Post shares valued at USD 492.3 million, bought Perfection Pet Foods for USD 235.0 million in December 2023, and in fiscal 2025 bought Potato Products of Idaho for USD 120.0 million and the rest of 8th Avenue for USD 798.8 million, which included retiring its debt and was funded with cash and revolver borrowings. It then sold 8th Avenue's pasta business on December 1, 2025 for a preliminary USD 375.0 million, receiving USD 378.5 million at closing while the buyer took on USD 78.2 million of leaseback liabilities, and sold Crystal Farms on May 1, 2026 for a preliminary USD 50.0 million, receiving USD 45.7 million at closing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_post-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 117–119; 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 12; calculation C17; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three note issues since October 2024 pushed maturities out and raised either coupons or principal. On October 9, 2024 Post issued USD 600.0 million of senior notes due 2034 at par and used part of the proceeds to redeem its notes due 2028. On December 15, 2025 it issued USD 1,300.0 million of 6.50% notes due 2036 at par and redeemed all USD 1,235.0 million of its 5.50% notes due 2029 for a premium of USD 22.6 million, a coupon 1.00 percentage points higher. On March 13, 2026 it issued a further USD 600.0 million of the 2034 notes at 100.75% of par and used the proceeds to repay the revolver. The notes are guaranteed by the domestic subsidiaries other than immaterial, excluded and unrestricted ones.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two events after the quarter end are kept outside the period figures. Post repurchased shares for USD 39.3 million between July 1 and August 5, 2026, leaving USD 490.7 million of authorization, and it expects to sell its Cobourg and Ashton-under-Lyne facilities in the second half of calendar 2026, with no proceeds stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Module status: Ready with Limitations. External sources: none used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor and governance risk level: Medium. The level is driven by repurchases above free cash flow and the absence of a stated financial policy, because cash is directed to shareholders ahead of debt reduction, which implies slower deleveraging and more refinancing dependence. Countervailing evidence is no dividend, no sponsor fees, early refinancings and clean audit opinions. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the indentures and management's stated leverage policy.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: This answer covers the fundamental credit profile of Post Holdings, Inc. (issuer id post) as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. It combines the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance work with the seven supplied filings and releases, the latest dated 2026-08-06. It draws no security, legal-capacity or position-sizing conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Post presents an adequate business profile with a weak financial policy: steady cash flow services high leverage, but cash repurchases ran at 2.28x free cash flow in nine months, so creditors depend on management restraining shareholder returns.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-09-30_post-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 96; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt was USD 7,367.0 million at June 30, 2026, or USD 7,406.3 million pro forma for USD 39.3 million of repurchases between July 1 and August 5, 2026, which is 5.33x reported EBITDA, or 5.36x pro forma. Liquidity of USD 1,242.4 million and no maturity before fiscal 2027 give a runway of at least a year, so the main risk is leverage rising on lower earnings, not a liquidity gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 17, 21; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ex99-1q32026er.htm.jsonl, page 6; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is large and spread widely enough to give reasonable cash-flow visibility, but reported growth overstates underlying demand. Net sales were USD 8,412.5 million over the last twelve months across four segments, and no customer exceeds 17.4% of sales, yet pet food supplied USD 890.6 million, or 76.3%, of the USD 1,167.1 million rise in sales between fiscal 2023 and fiscal 2025, and in nine months to June 2026 Post Consumer Brands sales fell 8.6% without 8th Avenue while pet food sales fell 15.0%. Creditors are relying on acquired earnings that are already shrinking organically.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_post-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 157; 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 33; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C21; calculation C22; calculation C23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Pricing power is limited and buyers hold most of the leverage. The largest customers are 29.9% of Post Consumer Brands, 33.0% of Weetabix, 42.0% of Foodservice and 34.9% of Refrigerated Retail, management expects the ready-to-eat cereal category to stay weak, and pet food prices fell on mix and promotion. Eggs are the exception only because avian influenza outbreaks lifted prices: that pricing raised Foodservice profit by USD 91.6 million, or 29.7%, in fiscal 2025 and is now lapping, so third-quarter Foodservice sales fell 6.5% and its profit fell 18.6%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_post-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 76, 155; 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 26, 33–34; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ex99-1q32026er.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C24; calculation C25

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins have held at group level, but the mix beneath them is moving and the main cost pressures are external. Reported EBITDA margin was 16.0% in fiscal 2024, 16.3% in fiscal 2025 and 16.4% over the last twelve months, helped in the nine months to June 2026 by USD 198.0 million of lower raw material costs in Foodservice, mainly eggs. Tariffs and the conflict in Iran have raised input, energy and freight costs, and management plans USD 80 million to USD 90 million of cage-free and precooked egg expansion, so margins depend on items management does not control.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_post-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 29, 34; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ex99-1q32026er.htm.jsonl, page 7; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is moderate and flattered in the latest period because capital spending fell. Free cash flow was USD 553.1 million over the last twelve months, 40.0% of reported EBITDA against 36.7% in fiscal 2025, after USD 439.5 million of capital expenditure and USD 370.1 million of cash interest in fiscal 2025. Nine-month free cash flow rose to USD 401.5 million from USD 336.5 million because additions to property fell, not because operating cash flow rose, and the split of capital spending between maintenance and growth is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_post-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 96, 128; 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is high and barely falling, and cover is thinner than the issuer's own ratios suggest. Net debt of USD 7,367.0 million at June 30, 2026 is 5.33x reported EBITDA, or USD 7,406.3 million and 5.36x pro forma for USD 39.3 million of repurchases between July 1 and August 5, 2026, against 5.45x at September 30, 2025. The issuer reports 4.6x net leverage and 3.8x interest cover on credit-agreement Adjusted EBITDA, but add-backs are 16.84% of reported EBITDA, reported EBITDA covered interest expense 3.30x over the last twelve months, and principal debt rose USD 223.8 million in nine months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 17; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ex99-1q32026er.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 22; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C9; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and the near maturity profile are the main supports, and the longer wall is the refinancing risk. Cash and undrawn revolver capacity were USD 1,242.4 million at June 30, 2026 before the later repurchases, 2.16x the USD 576.3 million falling due in fiscal 2027, of which USD 575.0 million is convertible notes due in August 2027 with a conversion price about 19.5% above the average price Post paid for shares after the quarter end. USD 4,566.0 million, or 59.5% of principal, falls due in fiscal 2030 to fiscal 2033, and refinancing the two lowest-coupon issues at the 6.50% coupon of the December 2025 notes would add about USD 45.6 million of interest a year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18, 20–21; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ex99-1q32026er.htm.jsonl, page 6; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C18; calculation C19; calculation C20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is the weakest dimension. Cash repurchases ran at 2.28x free cash flow in nine months to June 2026 and 1.45x in fiscal 2025, the board has approved four authorizations since August 2025, no leverage target is stated, and no sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed to support or constrain the issuer. Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk as Medium, and the one financial covenant tests secured net leverage only when revolver usage passes 30% of commitments, so it is untested at current usage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 23; 10-K_2025-09-30_post-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 96; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C14; calculation C32

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The realistic downside is leverage drifting up on lower egg earnings, not a liquidity event. If Foodservice earnings fell back to the USD 500 million run rate management describes and about USD 20 million of divested earnings left, Adjusted EBITDA would settle near management's comparable fiscal 2027 base of about USD 1.48 billion, USD 135.9 million or 8.4% below the last twelve months. With pro forma net debt of USD 7,406.3 million unchanged, reported-basis net leverage would rise from 5.36x to 5.94x, and free cash flow would fall to about USD 417.2 million, so using the USD 490.7 million of authorization left would exceed it by USD 73.5 million. Liquidity still covers the 2027 convertible notes, and management can stop repurchases, trim capital spending toward the USD 370 million to USD 390 million guided for fiscal 2026, or sell facilities, so distress is not the expected outcome.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ex99-1q32026er.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 21; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C29; calculation C30; calculation C31; calculation C17; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 12 months to 24 months the outlook is flat earnings, with the convertible notes due in August 2027 the one dated test. Management narrowed fiscal 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to USD 1,560 million to USD 1,570 million, which implies a fourth quarter of USD 369.5 million to USD 379.5 million against USD 425.4 million a year earlier, and describes fiscal 2027 as generally flat on a comparable base. Tailwinds are lower egg costs, Weetabix margin gains and lower capital spending; headwinds are pet food distribution losses, a weak cereal category, higher coupons on refinanced debt and the refinancing wall in fiscal 2030 to fiscal 2033. Over 3 years to 5 years the open questions are whether cereal and pet food volumes stabilise and whether that wall is refinanced at coupons above those it replaces.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ex99-1q32026er.htm.jsonl, pages 4–7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 34; calculation C28; calculation C29; calculation C18; calculation C19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against caution is cash and time: USD 1,242.4 million of liquidity, no revolver drawings, no maturity before fiscal 2027 and free cash flow of USD 553.1 million, with segment profit up 9.1% over nine months and repurchases that the board can stop. The view would improve if repurchases fell to the level of free cash flow and net debt began to fall, if Foodservice held earnings above the USD 500 million run rate, or if the 2027 convertible notes were settled from cash without new borrowing. It would worsen if fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA came in at the low end of the USD 369.5 million to USD 379.5 million implied range while repurchases stayed above free cash flow, or if revolver usage rose toward the 30% level at which the leverage covenant applies.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 23, 26–27; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ex99-1q32026er.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; calculation C17; calculation C12; calculation C27; calculation C28; calculation C32

fields.value: Liquidity covers the nearest maturity twice over. Cash and undrawn revolver capacity of USD 1,242.4 million compare with USD 576.3 million due in fiscal 2027, so a cash-settled convertible does not depend on market access and no refinancing is forced in the next twelve months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and customer spread cushion a single shock. Net sales of USD 8,412.5 million come from four segments and the largest customer is 17.4% of sales, so the loss of one account or one product line is partly absorbed by the others.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation is steady. Free cash flow of USD 553.1 million, 40.0% of reported EBITDA, covers interest and capital spending with a surplus that would repay debt if repurchases stopped.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C12; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns outrun cash generation. Cash repurchases were 2.28x free cash flow in nine months while principal debt rose USD 223.8 million, so each further quarter at that pace adds to net debt and delays deleveraging.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 17; calculation C14; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is high and the fall from 5.45x to 5.33x is small. Net debt of USD 7,367.0 million, USD 7,406.3 million pro forma, leaves little room for an earnings decline: a fall of USD 135.9 million in EBITDA would lift reported-basis net leverage to 5.94x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C4; calculation C29; calculation C30

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Organic sales are shrinking in the largest segment. Post Consumer Brands sales fell 8.6% in nine months without 8th Avenue and pet food sales fell 15.0%, so acquired earnings erode and revenue visibility is lower than the headline suggests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 33; calculation C22; calculation C23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings lean on an egg price cycle. Foodservice produced 38.5% of nine-month segment profit and management puts about USD 60 million of its fiscal 2026 earnings above a USD 500 million run rate, so a reversal lowers EBITDA without any change in debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 26; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ex99-1q32026er.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C26; calculation C29

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing will cost more. The 2030 and 2031 senior notes carry lower coupons than the 6.50% paid in December 2025, and refinancing them at that coupon would add about USD 45.6 million of interest a year against interest that already takes 30.3% of reported EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_post-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 19; calculation C19; calculation C10

fields.value: - No ratings, market prices or peer data are supplied, so the business profile is judged against its own history and relative value is not assessed; severity Medium; ratings and peer data would close it.

fields.value: - The credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so covenant headroom, the guarantee perimeter around Weetabix and capacity for distributions are not established; severity Medium; the executed documents would close it.

fields.value: - Management's USD 500 million Foodservice run rate has no stated earnings measure, so the USD 60 million above it cannot be tied to a reported line; severity Low; management commentary would close it.

fields.value: - The scenario assumes lost EBITDA reduces free cash flow dollar for dollar before tax and working capital, which overstates the cash effect; severity Low; a tax and working-capital forecast would close it.

fields.value: - Capital spending is not split into maintenance and growth, so the capital lever in the downside is not sized; severity Low; the fiscal 2026 annual report may close it.
